sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier resembles that of Promirotermes holmgreni, but the alates differ clearly. It is easily distinguished from the soldiers of the other two species of Promirotermes: the labrum of holmgreni and its varieties is much shorter, and according to Wasmann the anterior margin of the pronotum is deeply concave in dellicosi.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body length (with wings) 11.5—12 mm. Body dark brown above, the clypeal plate reddish brown, antennae, maxillary palps and legs yellowish brown, wings smoky brown. Head slightly longer than the width between the compound eyes; frons slightly flattened before and behind the imaginary line through the two ocelli, with a punctate fontanelle; compound eyes moderately convex; ocelli small, their distance from the margin of the compound eye about equal to their diameter; posterior margin of the clypeal plate strongly curved, the anterior margin only weakly arcuate; upper surface of the head fairly densely covered with long and short setae. Antennae 15-segmented, the first segment about twice as long as the second, the third as long as the second, the fourth slightly shorter and as long as wide, the fifth and sixth as long as the second or third. Mandibular dentition as shown in figures II: 3 and 4 of the original. Pronotum 0.56 mm long and 0.96 mm wide, rather flat, the anterior corners and the posterior margin only very slightly inclined downwards, the anterior margin narrow and raised; an oval pit on each side at the junction of the anterior and posterior lobes; margins and upper surface with numerous long and short setae; anterior corners broad and gently rounded, the posterior margin not concave. Mesonotum and metanotum narrowing posteriorly far less than in Mirotermes holmgreni as recorded in the original; posterior margin concave, forming an obtuse angle. Wings similar to those of M. holmgreni, densely covered with minute stellate hairs; in the forewing the radial sector, media and cubitus are separate from the scale onwards, in the hindwing the media arises from the radial sector; media and cubitus together with about 14—16 veins running to the posterior margin of the wing. Fore tibia with 3 apical spurs, mid and hind tibiae with 2 each. Abdomen broad, tergites 2—4 about half as long as the remaining tergites, densely hairy with long and short setae.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length (with mandibles) 5 mm; head length (with mandibles) 3.3 mm, head length (without mandibles) 1.63 mm; mandible length 1.72—1.75 mm; antennal length 2.47 mm. Body white, head pale yellow, mandibles black, abdomen without dark intestinal contents. Head cubical, the corners rounded, the sides narrowing forwards; frontal projection without a nasus or horns, rounded and blunt, similar to the frontal projection of Cubitermes soldiers; fontanelle situated below it and covered with setae. Labrum (measured between the tips of the two processes) as long as wide, the median notch deep, its depth as a proportion of the total length given in the original as "°/", defective in the OCR (see the note); the midline of the labrum slightly concave, the two halves swollen. Antennae (figure II: 7) 2.47 mm long, 14-segmented, the first segment less than twice the second, the lengths of segments 2 to 5 in the ratio 7:9:7:9, each segment distinctly longer than wide, pale yellow. Mandibles (figure II: 6) broadly as in Mirotermes, the right slightly longer than the left, with a cylindrical tooth at the base sharpened only at its very tip; the tips of both mandibles narrowed and curved inwards into a hook. Anterior lobe of the pronotum raised, without a distinct median depression. Abdomen with distinct short cerci; setae sparse except posteriorly.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body white, head and thorax faintly yellowish; abdomen with dark intestinal contents; antennae 14-segmented; hind tibia 1 mm long, body length 4 mm.

note: Adapted from Schmitz's 1917 German description of the new species; the original has three sections, alate, soldier and worker (Imago alata, Soldat, Arbeiter), described on pp. 227—230. Only legible figures are taken from the original: OCR misreadings such as "I2" (i.e. 12) and ":172—1:.75" (read as 1.72—1.75 mm after the Mandibeln of the same line) are given with the values unchanged. Lines severely damaged in the OCR and therefore not entered in the text: for the alate, "body length (without wings)" reads "> > > ohne Rluseliers te 5—5.5 >" (the figures 5—5.5 and the ditto structure are legible, the rest of the line is damaged), "body width" reads "7, 2%", "head length to the base of the epistoma" reads "OOF ta", "head width (between the inner margins of the compound eyes)" reads "O87 22", "antennal length" reads "2.5...", "hind tibia" reads "1.572"; for the soldier two further measurement lines read "OEE in: ... 2. 22mm" and "Buinserder ... 123mm", their labels illegible, and are not included; the depth of the median labral notch is given in the original as "°/", also damaged. None of these has been conjecturally restored. The original names the comparison for the mesonotum and metanotum "Mirotermes Holmgreni", which is transcribed as printed.
